hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis is missed or a procedure goes wrong at a Taft-area medical facility, the aftermath can be confusing and isolating. We help Taft residents understand California's medical malpractice rules and explore your options at no cost to start.

about.title: Taft Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Taft is a small community, and many residents rely on a limited number of local clinics and Kern County medical facilities for care they trust to be handled correctly. When that trust is broken — through a delayed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication error — the consequences can follow a person for years. Because Taft doesn't have the density of hospitals found in larger cities, malpractice claims here often involve travel to Bakersfield or other regional facilities for treatment, records, or follow-up procedures, adding complexity to an already stressful situation. California's medical malpractice laws, known as MICRA, set specific rules for how and when these claims must move forward. A bad medical outcome by itself doesn't mean malpractice occurred; the law requires proof that a provider's care fell below an accepted standard. Our team can review what happened and explain the options available under California law, at no charge.
commonInjuries: Misdiagnosis or delayed diagnosis of a serious condition
Surgical errors, including wrong-site or retained-instrument mistakes
Birth injuries to mother or newborn
Failure to monitor or follow up on abnormal test results

whyChoose.title: What Taft Residents Should Know About These Claims

items.title: Strict Filing Windows Apply
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims to be filed within one year of discovering the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened. Missing these deadlines can end a claim before it's reviewed, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider must typically receive 90 days' written notice. Our team can help make sure this step is handled correctly so it doesn't delay or derail the process.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: California law generally requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim, confirming that the care fell below an accepted standard. This is part of why early involvement can matter to your case.

items.question: Does Taft's smaller size affect where a malpractice claim gets handled?
items.answer: Not for the legal process itself, but many Taft residents receive treatment at facilities in Bakersfield or elsewhere in Kern County, which can mean records and providers are spread across more than one location. Our team can help gather documentation from all relevant facilities as part of reviewing the case.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome the same as malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves uncertainty, so a poor result alone isn't enough to prove malpractice. A claim generally requires showing that a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, which is why expert review is typically part of the process.

items.question: How much does it cost to speak with our team?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
